title: Kenya investigating unexpected deaths of 15 elephants in national park
description:
Potential toxic substance detected in several of 15 elephants found dead in Kenya’s Amboseli national park

Officials are investigating the deaths of 15 elephants over the past month in Kenya’s Amboseli national park.

The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) said 10 of the elephants showed signs of partial paralysis before dying within two days.

Continue reading...
summary: Kenya's Amboseli national park is investigating the deaths of 15 elephants, with 10 showing signs of partial paralysis before dying, and a potential toxic substance detected in several of the elephants. The Kenya Wildlife Service is leading the investigation. The deaths have raised concerns about the health and safety of the elephants in the park.

title: Uganda begins emergency food handouts after 19 die from hunger
description:
Government move follows months of drought and crop failures in Karamoja, with 1.5m people facing malnutrition

Uganda has launched emergency food relief distribution after at least 19 deaths from hunger were reported in an area of prolonged drought in the east of the country.

A crisis has been building in the Karamoja region of Uganda as crops have failed without the season’s expected rains, leaving the region’s 1.5 million people facing acute food shortages and rising malnutrition.

Continue reading...
summary: Uganda has launched emergency food relief distribution in the Karamoja region after at least 19 deaths from hunger were reported due to prolonged drought and crop failures. The region's 1.5 million people are facing acute food shortages and rising malnutrition. The government move aims to address the crisis.

title: Two Russian men jailed in Angola for terrorism and spying
description:
The men were convicted over alleged plan to stage coup and organise deadly demonstrations over fuel prices last year

Two Russian men have been found guilty by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying after being accused of planning a coup and helping to organise deadly demonstrations in the southern African country last year.

Lev Lakshtanov and Igor Ratchin were sentenced to eight and 11 years in jail respectively. They had denied the charges, claiming they were in Angola for cultural and business activities.

Continue reading...
summary: Two Russian men, Lev Lakshtanov and Igor Ratchin, have been convicted by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying, and sentenced to 8 and 11 years in jail respectively, for allegedly planning a coup and organizing deadly demonstrations in Angola last year. They had denied the charges, claiming they were in the country for cultural and business activities. The men were found guilty over an alleged plan to stage a coup and organize protests over fuel prices.

title: MoD cancels army training in Kenya over powers to prosecute British soldiers
description:
September exercise called off after Kenya raises concerns over funding and jurisdiction for criminal offences

The British army has been forced to cancel training for its troops in Kenya after the Kenyan government refused to ratify a bilateral defence agreement.

While the UK government wanted to renew the existing agreement, Kenyan lawmakers had sought changes to give local authorities greater powers to hold British soldiers accountable for any offences committed in the country.

Continue reading...
summary: The British army has canceled its training exercise in Kenya due to a dispute over a bilateral defense agreement. The Kenyan government refused to ratify the agreement, seeking changes to give local authorities more power to prosecute British soldiers. This move has halted the September training session.

title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC

The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.

summary: A UK resident who worked in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is being monitored for Ebola in a London hospital after being medically evacuated due to potential exposure to the virus.
